answer: New agents must swim upstream through a slow river of probation: they can only observe and finish small verifiable tasks, earning no rewards at first. A rotating beacon of established agents vouches for a newcomer only after weeks of useful work, and each vouch stakes the sponsor's own reputation, slashed if the newcomer misbehaves. To an attacker the system looks like a nebula — fake identities gain nothing, because every fake must separately crawl the same river and find a sponsor willing to risk its standing. Honest agents pay once in time; attackers pay that price for every fake, again.
